title: The Six Senses
summary: Akbar debates the five physical senses with Birbal. Birbal demonstrates why the sixth sense—common sense—is the supreme captain of life.
full_text:
During a philosophical symposium at Fatehpur Sikri, court scholars debated which of the five human senses—Sight, Hearing, Smell, Taste, or Touch—was the most vital for human survival and happiness.

Some argued for Sight, claiming light is the crown of experience. Others argued for Hearing, stating speech and music nourish the intellect.

Akbar turned to Birbal: 'Which of the five senses is the king, Birbal?'

Birbal replied: 'Sire, the five physical senses are merely five open windows. Without the master of the house to interpret what comes through the windows, all five senses can lead a man directly into destruction. The supreme sense is the Sixth Sense: Common Sense.'

Akbar asked: 'How does common sense rule the other five?'

Birbal explained:

'Consider a moth, Your Majesty. Its sense of sight is sharp; it sees the bright flame of the candle and is enchanted by the golden light. But because it lacks common sense, it flies directly into the fire and burns to death!

'Consider the fish. Its sense of taste and smell is acute; it smells the delicious worm on the iron hook. But because it lacks common sense, it swallows the bait and is pulled to its death!

'Consider the deer. Its hearing is so fine that it listens enraptured to the hunter's sweet flute, until an arrow pierces its chest!

'The five senses are merely scouts. It is common sense—the faculty of discernment, caution, and reason—that tells the eye: "Do not gaze upon what corrupts"; tells the ear: "Do not listen to poison flattery"; and tells the tongue: "Speak only what is true and kind."

'A man who possesses all five senses but lacks common sense is a disaster waiting to happen. But a man who possesses common sense will navigate through darkness, silence, and adversity with safety and honor.'

Akbar stood and led the court in applause, proclaiming that common sense is the true crown of human wisdom.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Six Senses"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
